title: Login service with a redacting JSON logger
name: Login event logging

locateQuestion.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code produces its structured login logs? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
locateQuestion.explanation: There is no defect. with() copies bindings into a new object, so per-request context never leaks between requests. Errors go through serializeError, which reads name, message and stack explicitly (they are not enumerable on Error, so spreading would lose them). The success log includes the whole session object, which looks risky, but redact() walks nested objects and replaces the token key with "[redacted]"; the password is never passed to the logger. level, event and time are written after the spread, so caller fields cannot overwrite them.

choiceQuestions.prompt: What does the 'login.succeeded' line contain for the session field?
choices: Nothing; session is dropped because it is an object
An object with token set to "[redacted]" and the real expiresAt
The string "[redacted]" in place of the whole session
choiceQuestions.explanation: redact() recurses into the session object; only the key 'token' is in REDACTED_KEYS, so it is replaced while expiresAt is kept. 'session' itself is not a redacted key, so the object is not replaced wholesale, and objects are not dropped.

choiceQuestions.prompt: Credentials.verify rejects with new Error("db timeout"). What does the caller receive and what is logged?
choices: { ok: false, reason: "unavailable" }, and an error line with err.type, err.message and err.stack
The exception propagates to the caller and nothing is logged
{ ok: false, reason: "invalid_credentials" }, and a warn line
{ ok: false, reason: "unavailable" }, and an error line whose err field is an empty object
choiceQuestions.explanation: The catch around verify calls log.error with the error, which serializeError turns into { type, message, stack } by reading those properties directly, then returns reason 'unavailable'. The exception is not rethrown; 'invalid_credentials' is the null-user path.

choiceQuestions.prompt: Two logins for different tenants run concurrently through the same LoginService. Can one request's log lines carry the other's tenantId?
choices: Yes, because this.log is shared across requests
No, because with() returns a new logger with a freshly built bindings object
Yes, if the second request starts before the first logs
Only for error lines, since error() adds fields
choiceQuestions.explanation: with() constructs a new JsonLogger whose bindings are a new object made by spreading, and the shared root logger is never mutated. Each login uses its own local log. Sharing the root is safe because it is read-only here, and error() also only builds new objects.
